newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -June 25.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -June 25.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising,
Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and
Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
BONN - Germany's advertising industry fears that increasing
regulatory pressure on tobacco manufacturers will lead to more
restrictions on tobacco advertising. The ZAW German Federation
of Advertisers says tobacco companies should continue to have
the right to advertise and that present legal and
self-regulatory restrictions are already tight enough. (Reuter)
WALLDORF - The DF1 channel, struggling to make an impact on
Germany's commercial pay-TV market, has invited five agencies to
pitch for a 60-million-mark ($34.8-million) ad. Eighteen
agencies were initially considered. (Kress)
FRANKFURT - German agencies failed to win any Press and Poster
awards at the International Advertising Festival in Cannes, with
only Berlin-based Scholz & Friends managing to make a shortlist
for its ad campaign for the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung
newspaper. Leo Burnett in London won the Grand Prix for its
Mercedes-Benz ad. (Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
BONN - ANGA, the federation of German private cable operators,
wants state media authorities to have less say in determining
which channels are given space on existing bandwidth. ANGA says
just six channels -- national public channels ARD and ZDF, one
further public channel per region and the top three commercial
stations -- should be guaranteed space by the authorities, with
cable network operators themselves then choosing the rest. At
present, the shortage of bandwidth space has meant media
authorities have the final say on overall allocation. (Reuter)
HAMBURG - Should Kirch and Bertelsmann-affiliate CLT-Ufa run
into cartel problems with their planned cooperation, they appear
to have won some political backing for their cause. Wolfgang
Clement, Economics Minister in the large state of North
Rhine-Westphalia, says recent federal cartel office criticism of
the deal is premature. Clement told the "Die Woche" newspaper
that any appraisal of the agreement could only follow the
signing of contracts by the two. (Reuter)
MUNICH - TV-shopping channel H.O.T. is to add a further 560,000
cable households to its coverage from July by gaining a licence
in the large southern German state of Baden-Wuerttemberg. The
licence means some 9.4 million households in Germany and Austria
can receive the channel. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
HAMBURG - Tobacco group Reemtsma is looking to maintain its
growth rates in future with acquisitions in Eastern Europe and
Asia. Management board chairman Ludger Staby says the group is
already the world's fastest growing cigarette producer and is
targeting 10 percent sales growth for the current year. Sales
target for 1997 is 120 billion cigarettes, he says. (Reuter)
BRUSSELS - Sales of Daimler-Benz AG cars climbed 11 percent in
the first five months of this year to more than 20.4 billion
marks, according to Juergen Hubbert, the head of Daimler's car
operations. Hubbert says demand for the A-class model, Daimler's
first foray into compact cars, had been strong and the company
sold the 28,000 models it plans to make this year in the first
few days they were available. The company still plans, however,
to produce 180,000 A-Class cars in 1998. Daimler plans to
produce a total of 700,000 cars this year, up from 645,000 in
1996. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Eurocheques are facing an uncertain future as one of
Germany's most popular and well-known means of paying for
medium-sized transactions, a new study shows. Research
commissioned recently by Germany's banks noted a steady decline
in usage of Eurocheques in favour of cash and credit cards,
partly encouraged by the banks themselves. But banks, especially
those whose business is driven by customers who don't like to
use plastic cards, insist there are no concerted plans to
effectively scrap cheque-based transactions. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
WALLDORF - Georg Flandorfer, 50, is named new head of
distribution for VW unit Audi. (Kress)
FRANKFURT - Hans Kratz, 53, chairman of the OWM federation of
German brand advertisers, is to quit Henkel as head of its
advertising to join Mediahaus Stroebel in Duesseldorf.
(Horizont)
